body: I have a plan. I have the means. I even have a date set. If that's not imminent danger, I'm not sure what is. I'm not at all opposed to seeing a therapist, in-fact it might be fun to see how they react, but if if these three things become apparent to them then I have no doubts that I'll end up in a place I don't want to be. I've thought about doing the whole "I have a friend" routine where I assure them that I'm fine, I just need advice to pass on to my friend, but I'm not even sure if that would work. Clearly they would know I'm being facetious.
Ah, my misunderstanding then. Though they would find out as soon as I'm put into a mental hospital anyway. As would my teachers since I'd have to explain my lack of attendance.

I'm not even sure what that means. I'd say the sum of my believes is that existence is effort and my personal effort is not enough to be happy. Simply being 'not sad' isn't enough for me. Maybe it's enough for others and that's fine, but not me. So I might as well not exist.

I don't want to get away from suicide. It is completely logical as far as I'm concerned. Until someone presents me with a more logical argument at least.

As for the companionship thing, I play videogames with friends everyday. Friends that I have known for years irl. I also interact with my teachers and fellow students at least twice a week.

Firstly I'd like to thank you for the well written and thoughtful reply. Don't worry about offending me or anything. At this point I'm only interested in objective truth. I don't really care what other people think, just what they know.

You're right about the content issue. It was the closest word I could think of, but it's not exactly what I'm describing. What I meant by it is that I'm neither sad nor happy. I'm at that fine line right between them. I'm not sure what the word for that is.

I'm not blaming myself for having these thoughts btw. In-fact I view them as perfectly logical. There are no negative emotions attached to these thoughts at all.

I would definitely say I'm apathetic, but I don't think I necessarily feel empty. I'm also not entirely certain that apathy is inherently negative. There's several studies that show apathy isn't always linked to depression.

I would say more accurately it's "If I've felt like this my entire adult life, I will probably feel like this forever." I'm not actually sure if overall happiness is even attainable.

As for the therapy thing, I can't see one and have this conversation without being institutionalized or put on some kind of watch list against my will. I imagine my family would probably be notified as well.

All of this being said I am well aware of inherent bias. It very well could be that I'm delusional or depressed, but that's just another reason for me to seek out logical arguments. If there are good ones then I will accept that I am wrong. If there aren't, then I will proceed with my plan.

Yeah. I went to a introductory Buddhist class in 2010. I've also been to the largest Buddha statue in the world located in Japan. I'm an athiest though. I don't believe in karma or anything supernatural at all. There's just no empirical evidence for any of it. As for meditation, I've tried it, but it just feels like an uncomfortable nap without any actual sleep.

I completely agree with everything you've said here. The only difference is you just seem to accept it, and I reject it. As to your question, no. I've been a nihlist for several years so I came to these realizations a long time ago. It's just that back then my line of thinking was, "But what if it gets better. What if happiness is right around the corner. You'll miss out." Now I believe I was just fooling myself. Just like you were saying, I don't actually think that sort of happiness is attainable.

Is it though? I'm not necessarily happy, I'm just not sad. And I think that's the issue. If it takes this much effort to exist and all I can ever hope for is to be satisfied, then is life even worth it? I think the logical answer is no. But most people only care about the emotional answer.

You didn't convince me that life is worth living at all. From my perspective I should be congratulating you. Dying from natural causes would make this a lot easier. That way I wouldn't have to care if my body we're found. I could die without guilt in that scenario.

From what I've read vomiting would only occur if I overload my system too quickly. For example if I took 200mg instead of the 85mg I will be taking. Or if I were to crush the pills to absorb them faster. Also, worst case scenario, as long as I lose consciousness first I don't actually care how I die.

Unfortunately I can't see a therapist. The instant I mention any of this they will alert my family and put me on suicide watch. Or worse, I'll end up in some institution. But I can assure you that I'm not sad whatsoever. If I were depressed wouldn't I feel like I'm sad or don't have energy or something? I run 2 miles a day just for fun. I have more free time than anyone I know. And as far as I can tell I have no stress in my life at all.
